stops.title: The exam in 2 minutes
stops.note: Format, scope, limits and the nine sample shapes. Read it once.

stops.title: Baseline: the teacher's sample paper
stops.note: Nine questions, 30 minutes, no notes. The score does not matter yet; it shows what you are up against.

stops.title: Process: lifecycle, Agile and Scrum
stops.note: Scenario judgement: lifecycle, Agile and Scrum. The words you choose matter.

stops.title: Tool errors and project setup
stops.note: A tool error and one sensible next step. Sample Q1 is this shape.

stops.title: Programs and the command line
stops.note: Typer argument or option, exit codes and what the entry point runs.

stops.title: Break
stops.note: Away from the screen. Water, food, a short walk. No notes.

stops.title: Clean-code problems
stops.note: Name the clean-code problem and say why it hurts a teammate.

stops.title: Refactoring or not
stops.note: Refactoring or not: does the behaviour change? Sample Q2 is this shape.

stops.title: mypy errors and the right fix
stops.note: Read one mypy error and pick the right fix. Sample Q3 and Q9.

stops.title: Core, shell and failing well
stops.note: Functional core, imperative shell, and failing loudly at the boundary.

stops.title: Break
stops.note: Stand up, eat something, drink water. The next block is tests and diffs.

stops.title: Failing tests, pytest and TDD
stops.note: A failing test line and what you can conclude. Sample Q4 is this shape.

stops.title: Diffs and commit messages
stops.note: Read a diff and judge two commit messages. Sample Q8.

stops.title: Writing the open answers
stops.note: Open answers: what to write in 5 to 8 lines. Sample Q7, Q8 and Q9.

stops.title: Paths, files and permissions
stops.note: Read a terminal transcript: paths, files and permissions.

stops.title: Pipes, text wrangling and bash scripts
stops.note: Pipes, text wrangling and bash scripts. Sample Q6 and Lab 10.

stops.title: Break
stops.note: Last break before the full papers. Clear your head, then sit them like the real thing.

stops.title: Paper A, realistic
stops.note: Sit it as on the day: 60 minutes, pen and paper for the open answers, no notes.

stops.title: Review Paper A
stops.note: Read every explanation, wrong or right. Mark the open answers against the rubric.

stops.title: Redo your mistakes
stops.note: Every question you got wrong so far, again.

stops.title: Paper C, worst case
stops.note: Longer artefacts, closer options. If you can do this one, the real paper is easier.

stops.title: Review Paper C
stops.note: Same routine: read every explanation, then mark the open answers.

stops.title: Say it on the paper
stops.note: The phrases to write, type by type. Read them out loud once.
